sources.entry: Glance - Highly customizable dashboard that puts all your feeds in one place. AGPL-3.0 Docker/Go
Glance | Lightweight dashboard that puts your feeds and services in one place

summary.one_liner: Glance is a lightweight, highly customizable self-hosted dashboard that displays RSS feeds, social/news sources, weather, markets, and service status on one YAML-configured page.
summary.what_it_does: Glance renders a configurable start page of widgets that pull in feeds and data, including RSS, subreddit posts, Hacker News, Lobsters, weather forecasts, YouTube channel uploads, Twitch channels, market prices, Docker container status, server stats, and GitHub releases. Layout and widgets are defined in YAML files, with multiple pages supported and columns sized small or full. Custom widgets can be built from iframe, html, extension (fetch HTML from a URL), and custom-api (fetch JSON and render with custom HTML) types. Data is fetched when a page loads and cached per widget, with no background polling, so a page refresh is needed to see new information. The README says it has low memory usage, few dependencies, and minimal vanilla JS.
use_cases: Personal news and feed reader start page
Monitoring Docker container status on a home server
Tracking stock and crypto prices on a dashboard
Watching YouTube and Twitch channels in one place
Showing weather and calendar on a home screen
Tracking GitHub release versions of selfhosted projects
how_to_run: mkdir glance && cd glance && curl -sL | tar -xzf - --strip-components 2
Edit docker-compose.yml, config/home.yml, and config/glance.yml as desired
docker compose logs (to check for issues)
Alternatively, with Go >= v1.23: go build -o build/glance . then run the binary (or use go run .)
notable: Single-binary deployment with precompiled builds for Linux, Windows, and macOS on x86, x86_64, ARM, and ARM64
Custom widget types: iframe, html, extension, and custom-api
Data fetched on page load and cached per widget rather than polled in the background
Community widgets, preconfigured pages, and themes mentioned in the README
caveats: Pages do not update automatically; a browser refresh is required to see new data
Ad-blocking DNS services such as Pi-Hole or AdGuard Home can cause request timeouts unless their rate limits are raised
Browser extension Dark Reader can break layout of some widgets
